data.narrative:
Nox Metals is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Zane Hengsperger that has raised $5.1M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises 9 private robotics and manufacturing firms and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the immediate peer set at identical stage and valuation tier remains thin.

Our valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology given insufficient depth in same-stage peer comparables. Using total capital raised ($5.1M) as a value proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement in the sector yields an implied valuation of $13M. A peer-median approach was not feasible: while 11 same-sector companies exist, only 1 shared Nox's exact stage and 1 occupied adjacent stage, falling short of the 3-company minimum for reliable median triangulation. Broader sector-wide comparisons would introduce unacceptable methodological noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M to $15M, with a median point of $13M. This reflects a 2.1x to 2.9x step-up from deployed capital, consistent with Seed-stage risk and early market validation. Key uncertainties include the durability of near-peer comparable multiples in a sector experiencing rapid consolidation, and the absence of recent downstream funding signals that might anchor stage-transition assumptions. Additional fundraising data or customer traction metrics would materially strengthen conviction.
